text:
sarah: quick ping 10min: nightly SAST exploded after automated KMS rotation + infra tidy. CI runner couldn't decrypt secrets and suppressions weren't applied. tagging @nate @cleo. keeping thread concise.

nate: on it. short hypothesis: key rotation changed the key resource name (we went from ci-secrets-v1 -> ci-secrets-v2) and the CI SA still only had IAM on the old key resource; also suppression bucket moved to a new project and the CI SA lost storage.objectViewer.

cleo: can you paste the failure lines from the scanner?

sarah: sure, runner stderr: 
```
2026-09-14T03:12:11Z key-wrapper: decrypt failed: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = requester does not have permission to access key projects/PRJ/locations/global/keyR/keys/ci-secrets-v2
2026-09-14T03:12:12Z scanner: failed to fetch suppressions: GET https://configs.internal/scan/suppressions.json 403
2026-09-14T03:12:14Z scanner: scanning anyway: alerts=74 (likely dupes on generated code)
```

infra-admin: infra tidy CR-2026-09-13 applied: rotated key ci-secrets -> ci-secrets-v2 and moved suppression configs to gs://configs-staging. Binding removal log shows group:old-ci-admins removed from project-storage and key ring.

nate: ok. mitigation plan: 1) ephemeral grant to CI SA for the new key and bucket; 2) re-run SAST to validate suppression fetch; 3) fix permanent IAM and add preflight checks. Example ephemeral commands: 
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/PRJ/locations/global/keyR/keys/ci-secrets-v2 \\
  --member=serviceAccount:ci-runner@prj.iam.gserviceaccount.com \\
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter --condition=None
gsutil iam ch serviceAccount:ci-runner@prj.iam.gserviceaccount.com:objectViewer gs://configs-staging
```

cleo: also check logging sink/filter. if someone excluded infra SAs we might not see decrypt audit events. audit-bot, any insights?

audit-bot: created ticket SEC-4100 (ephemeral grant + key-rotation-audit) and flagged audit-sink review.

infra-admin: applied ephemeral grants at 03:28. re-run started.

sarah: update: suppressions fetched & decrypt succeeded. SAST alerts dropped from 74 -> 6. KMS audit now shows Decrypt on ci-secrets-v2 by serviceAccount:ci-runner@prj at 03:28:39 UTC.

nate: good. follow-ups: 1) INFRA-4101: add permanent least-priv binding for ci-runner on ci-secrets-v2 and gs://configs-staging, document reason; 2) INFRA-4102: add an alert when KMS key resource name changes (rotation) so we proactively validate IAM bindings; 3) SEC-4103: GH preflight step that validates KMS decrypt + suppression fetch before scanning. Also: 4) update ops playbook to avoid removing key bindings in bulk during rotation.

cleo: small note: suppression strategy that relies on a single external bucket + single SA is brittle. Recommend adding a repo-level fallback suppress file and using signed URLs for the external store.

sarah: agree. I'll open SEC-4104 PR to add repo fallback and the GH preflight. nate, can you own INFRA-4101/4102?

nate: yep. I'll also add a quick script to list keys and compare expected resource names in CI before runs. gist snippet: 
```
# preflight: ensure expected key exists and CI SA binding present
gcloud kms keys list --location=global --keyring=keyR --project=PRJ | grep ci-secrets-v2
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy projects/PRJ/locations/global/keyR/keys/ci-secrets-v2
```

infra-admin: opening INFRA-4101/4102 and will attach audit evidence. note: we'll also tweak the logging sink filter that previously excluded "serviceAccount:old-*" patterns; will keep key/audit entries for infra principals.

audit-bot: updated SEC-4100 with links to INFRA tickets and assigned to nate + sarah.

sarah: quick postmortem note for sync: avoid bulk removal of key bindings during rotation; always run the CI preflight after rotation; avoid single-SA dependency for suppression fetch. short and blameless. thanks all :thumbsup: will close once PRs/tickets linked.
